outcome: Need for respiratory care in offspring
cohort: Women with epilepsy (WWE) who gave birth in Finland during 1987-2008 (n = 1737) and a reference cohort of a random sample of women without epilepsy (n = 4357)
finding: Women with epilepsy in Finland had an increased risk of complications and hospitalizations during pregnancy and delivery, including premature rupture of membranes, premature contractions, infections, induction of labor, cesarean section, and their offspring had an increased risk of being small for gestational age, needing admission to the neonatal intensive care unit, and requiring respiratory care.
mod_finding: The risk for induction of delivery or a cesarean section was increased in WWE.
